newsitem.title: USA: Triarc closes Snapple buy, cancels IPO plan.
newsitem.headline: Triarc closes Snapple buy, cancels IPO plan.

text.p: Triarc Cos Inc said Thursday it completed its $300 million acquisition of Snapple Beverage Corp from Quaker Oats Co.
The company also said it will not go forward with plans for an initial offering of about 20 percent of its beverage and restaurant business.
In a statement, the company cited the just-completed acquisition and "other complex issues" as leading it to abandon the initial public offering plans.
Triarc also said it expects the Snapple purchase to enhance its earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) for fiscal 1997.
It said Snapple, together with Mistic Brands and Royal Crown, will operate as part of its beverage group, which had sales of $310 million in 1996.
The conclusion of the deal closes the book on what proved to be a disastrous acquisition by Quaker, which bought Snapple more than two years ago in a deal valued at $1.8 billion.
Quaker recorded a $1.1 billion write-off charge in its first quarter on the Snapple business.
The dismal outcome led to criticism of Quaker's chairman William Smithburg, who last month announced plans to retire.
